content.text:
The mapper is written in `out/transform.ts`. It passes the strict type-check and runs cleanly on the sample patients. I also tried made-up cases in `out/scratch.ts`, including held and stopped lines, a drug-caused diagnosis, a CKD restage, a restricted problem, a cells/uL platelet count and a repeat BP, and on different `asOf` dates. Only the 10 samples are real data, so the made-up cases show the code does what I meant, not that it matches the source.

Judgment calls:

- **Corrections:** Any item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes`, `retracts` or `voided_items` is dropped, whatever the void reason. Lists are rebuilt from the remaining events only, so a voided item never affects another line.
- **Medications:**
  - The status comes only from the latest event per `med_id`, as the schema says. A `change` therefore counts as active even if it follows a hold.
  - `status_since` is the latest start or resume date for active lines, and the hold or stop date otherwise.
  - Lines for the same drug are merged into one row, keeping the line whose latest event is newest. The drug name is worked out from the source's display name: salts and leading amounts like "3 ML" are stripped, and brand names are looked up in a built-in table.
  - A dose in tablets is turned into mg or mcg when the product name gives a single strength per tablet. Combination products stay in tablets.
  - `rxnorm_ingredient` is never set, because Northgate only gives product-level RxNorm codes.
- **Problems:**
  - Resolved lines are reported as `resolved`; lines removed as wrong are dropped.
  - Lines with the same ICD code are merged into one row, and all CKD (N18) lines are merged into one row.
  - The CKD stage is read from the description first (e.g. "stage 3b"), then from the N18.x code. Albuminuria (A1–A3) is read only from the description.
  - Billing and referral diagnoses are ignored.
- **Drug-caused diagnoses:** Descriptions like "X-associated/induced …", "… due to <drug>" and "Adverse effect of …" also produce an allergy row. If only a drug class is named and it can't be narrowed to one drug, the class name is used. A matching allergy-list entry absorbs the class row instead of duplicating it. Criticality is left `unknown` because no one recorded it.
- **Allergies:**
  - The reaction type is decided from the reaction text first (hives or angioedema → hypersensitivity; ketoacidosis or hyperkalemia → serious adverse event; cough or GI upset → side effect), and only then from Northgate's own category.
  - Mechanism is `non_immune` for Northgate's intolerance and adverse-reaction entries and for ACE-inhibitor cough or angioedema. Entries labelled "allergy" get `unknown`, not `immune`, since the spec asks for proof.
- **Labs:**
  - Test type is identified by LOINC, then Northgate's code, then Lakeview's code, then the test name. Values whose unit isn't recognised are skipped.
  - Platelet and white-cell counts in cells/uL are divided by 1000.
  - The race-adjusted eGFR value is dropped whenever the same report also has the race-free one.
  - For the eGFR equation, the lab's method comment wins, then Lakeview's code, then LOINC. So the sample's MDRD LOINC with a "CKD-EPI 2009" comment gives `ckd-epi-2009`.
  - Non-numeric and withdrawn values are skipped. Copies of one result are kept once, preferring the most advanced status.
- **Vitals:** Every vital-sign set is a clinic row, timed at the item's effective time in Chicago local time. A repeat BP fills the `repeat_*` fields. Sets with only temperature, SpO2 or height produce no row, because the view has no fields for those.
